text: Ajoy Nath Ray, born on 31 October 1946 in Kolkata, is an Indian retired judge who served as the former Chief Justice of both the Allahabad and Sikkim High Courts. His father, Mr. A. N. Ray, was the 14th Chief Justice of India. Ray earned a degree in Science with Physics Honours from Calcutta University and completed his B.A. at the School of Jurisprudence, Oriel College, Oxford. He began practicing as an Advocate in civil matters at the Calcutta High Court on 4 August 1970 and was promoted to permanent Judge of the same court on 6 August 1990. On 6 June 2004, he assumed the role of Acting Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. He was appointed Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court on 11 January 2005 and later transferred to become Chief Justice of the Sikkim High Court on 27 January 2007. Ray retired from the judiciary on 30 October 2008. This Indian law–related biographical article is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by adding missing information.
